But I thought I would show you guys my outfit, so somebody saw it. Because I know I'll get questions. My dress is from Eloquii, but I got it from D&Co. My jacket is from Asos, and my boots are Topshop. It's a cute look. His loss. Guys, let's talk about catfishing and what to do when it happens to you. If you go on enough dates from dating apps, sooner or later it's probably going to happen. Whether you're a man or a woman, doesn't matter. You will see pictures of one person, and then someone quite different shows up in real life. Maybe 50 kilos heavier, 20 years older, or just nothing like their photos. So what do you do? First, figure out if it's really catfishing. Or if you just were not paying attention. If the person actually had realistic photos, and you ignored them, that is on you. You don't have to stay, but at least handle it gracefully. Have a short chat, maybe a quick drink, and then leave politely. No need to make someone feel worse, just keep your karma clean. But if it's actual catfishing, if the person clearly misled you, that's disrespectful. They wasted your time. In that case, you have every right to walk away. You can be polite, but firm. You can literally say, you look quite different from your photos, and I don't think it makes sense to continue. And let's be real, in this video, I wouldn't be shocked if she actually catfished a guy. Just look at how she framed the video. So maybe the guy stood her up, not because she's overweight, but because she hid it in her profile. Small tip, when you're scrolling through dating apps, always set your expectations by the worst photo. That's usually the closest to reality. Share your own catfishing stories in the comments.
